_comment: Dependency index for documents that MUST STAY CURRENT. Each entry names the authoritative
sources a document was derived from, and the date it was last checked against them.
Checked by scripts/docs/check_doc_sources.py — when a source changes after a document's
'reviewed' date, that document is flagged as possibly stale. See CORE.md section 5.
DELIBERATELY NOT INDEXED: docs/decisions/ and docs/contracts/. Those are point-in-time
records and frozen interfaces — they are superseded, never refreshed, so a staleness flag
on them would be noise. See .ai/skills/docs-author/references/DESIGN-DOC.md.
'reviewed' is an attestation ('someone read this against its sources on this date'), not an
edit date. Fixing a typo does not advance it; re-checking the content against the sources does.

docs.note: Sign-in model and roster/auth rules from PROJECT.md; the night-before due date rule from CORE.md section 2, whose HOUR is per-course policy (1759 phys-215, 2359 phys-110) — if a course changes it, this page is wrong; what the Lessons and Dashboard pages actually show from the student modules.

Student-facing promise about what AI does and does not decide. CORE.md section 6 governs 3-state grading, is_finalized=false, and the hidden diagnostics; the two skills define what actually gets written.

The 3-state toggle, question_scores shape, and the 'all my sections' scoping rule. If the Grade tab's behaviour changes, this doc is wrong before anything else is. nav.js is a source because the page has NO nav entry (P1.14, 2026-07-23) — the doc's 'getting to the Grade page' section is the only place that is written down, so a nav change silently invalidates it. grade.html is a source because the hand-grading queue is rendered there, not in the data module. faculty-tasks.js is a source since 2026-07-27: the due-out boxes are the documented route to this page, and they are now one box per assignment that deep-links into it, so a change to that registry invalidates the 'Getting to the Grade page' section. lessons.html is a source since 2026-07-29: the Assignments page now carries a Grade button that deep-links here, so it is one of the enumerated routes and a change to it invalidates the list.
Says in-page that CORE.md and PROJECT.md remain authoritative and that this page is the bug if they disagree — so it is the entry most likely to need a refresh when the contract moves.
Summarises the shared-state rules and the operating contract. Must never contain what SYSTEM_GUIDE.md may contain — help docs are public at every tier.
The authoring contract. Documents the renderer's actual behaviour — tier gating, the manifest fields, the no-front-matter Jekyll trap. Not served to users.

Course-director and system operating guide. Roles, edge functions, and admin procedures are defined in PROJECT.md and must agree. The two account edge functions are sources because the deploy list here is the ONLY complete one — a function written and not added to it is a function a from-scratch rebuild silently omits, which fails at the moment somebody cannot sign in.

The ordered PREP v2 cutover procedure. Derived step-for-step from the bootstrap SQL (roles, auth-FK, read window, seal) and the migration script (what moves, what is left behind, the frozen-slug check). If either changes, the runbook is wrong before anything else.

Encodes the help-doc mechanics (no front matter, start at ##, manifest fields, tier gating) and the docs/ taxonomy. If the renderer or the taxonomy changes, the skill teaches the wrong thing to every future author.

Conceptual companion to director-schema-reference.md, which owns the field-level detail and the enforced-rules list; this page links out rather than restating them, after a restated unlock rule drifted and contradicted the reference. Deliberately contains no UI procedures - it explains the model, not the screens, so a page rename cannot invalidate it. (This note used to justify that by saying site/app/ does not read the app schema yet; it has read it since 2026-07-21 - the reason stands, the justification did not.) faculty-lessons.js became a source on 2026-07-28: whether reusing an assignment SHARES it or COPIES it is the content model, not a screen, and it is decided in saveLesson() rather than in any migration - this page said 'schedule the same library entry again instead of copying it', which was true until that day and is now the opposite of what happens. The decision doc is listed beside it because it is where the reasoning lives.

Every table and field transcribed from the app-schema migrations and verified against information_schema on the live database. Owns the enforced-rules list and the exact accepted values. Inline SVG depends on the .sf-* classes in styles.css. Omits RLS policy predicates - help docs are world-readable at every tier. SOURCES MUST LIST EVERY MIGRATION: the list stopped at 006 until 2026-07-22, so 007-009 landed without ever flagging this page and analysis_runs went undocumented for two days. Add the new file here whenever a migration is added. ei_sessions states its staff-only access rule in plain language and nothing more: that absence of a student policy is load-bearing (notes may hold a candid read of a cadet), so do not delete the sentence - and do not 'complete' it by pasting the policy SQL either.

docs.why: The only documentation of the in-person password-reset workflow, which replaced email recovery on 2026-07-21, and of the registrar roster-export format. If reset-student-password's authorization or the importer's required columns change, this page misdirects an instructor standing in front of a locked-out cadet. Both pages are sources since 2026-07-23 (P1.9): reset lives on Roster and is an instructor action, import and provisioning live on Enrollment and are a director's — the doc sends the reader to one or the other by name, so a move between them makes it wrong. The three staff-password sources were added 2026-07-27, when a derivable default (last name + 1234) made a delegated staff reset possible: this page is now the only place the rule is written down for a human, and the derivation itself has three code copies that must agree.
